news.label: Tripo AI Teases H3.5
details: Compared with the earlier H3.1, it improves fine detail and visual fidelity, aiming to produce models that need minimal editing afterward.
Real mesh quality and printability will need to be checked once it's released.
A dedicated AI agent that bridges generated data to 3D printers was also announced.

news.label: Mimaki's 3D Printer, 1.4x Color Gamut
details: Mimaki Engineering's 3DUJ-553MkII is a full-color 3D printer that uses UV-curable inkjet technology.
It keeps the previous model's ability to show over ten million colors, while reproducing dark colors and surface patterns more faithfully.
A new ink for internal infill helps cut costs, and it also aims to make continuous printing more efficient.

news.label: NVIDIA on Sparse Attention
points: Narrowing down what to look at
details: A technical article has been published about designing Sparse Attention for LLMs that handle long contexts.
With regular attention, computation and memory access grow as the input gets longer, but with Sparse Attention each token looks at a narrower set of information.
It explains the idea of optimizing the model design and the GPU kernel implementation together.

lines.say: It explains sparse attention, a design that helps A I handle long text by focusing on less information and lightening the computation.

lines_timed.show: Good morning, and welcome to Mono Radio! It's Wednesday, November 18, and here are your morning headlines.
Today we have five new announcements from the worlds of AI and 3D.
Let's start with OpenAI. Two new models are here: Astra and Sol, part of GPT-6.2.
Astra is better at 3D design and code fixes, and it costs 20 percent less than the previous model.
Next up, a new model from Tripo AI called H3.5.
It's at the teaser stage and aims to generate printable shapes. A dedicated agent to connect to printers was announced too.
Now for some real hardware. Mimaki Engineering has announced a new full-color 3D printer.
Its color gamut is about 1.4 times wider, so dark colors and surface patterns look more lifelike.
Up next, a technical article from NVIDIA.
It explains Sparse Attention, a design that helps AI handle long text by focusing on less information and lightening the load.
Last up is 3D Systems, with a new MultiJet printer and a powder management system for metal.
They're aiming for better efficiency across not just the printer, but materials and data management too.
Our pick of the day is Tripo AI's H3.5. We can't wait to see if it grows into 3D models you can truly print.
That's all for now. See you next time on Mono Radio!
